samples: This program reads a question from the command-line arguments and an API key from the `CHAT_API_KEY` environment variable, sends the question as a single user message to a chat-completions HTTP endpoint (a placeholder `api.example.com` URL with a placeholder model name), and prints the text of the model's first answer. It needs console, environment, and network access. If the key is missing, the response has no choices, or the request or parsing fails, it exits with a descriptive error instead of printing an answer. Before you use it, you would need to change the endpoint and model name to a real service and check that the service accepts this request and response format.

This program reads a question from the command-line arguments and an API key from the `CHAT_API_KEY` environment variable, sends the question as a single user message to a chat-completions endpoint at a placeholder URL (api.example.com) with a placeholder model name, and prints the text of the first answer. It needs console, environment and network access, and it fails with a clear error if the key is missing, the model returns no choices, or the HTTP or JSON step goes wrong. Before using it, you would need to replace the endpoint and model name with real ones. Also note that it is strictly one question and one answer, with no conversation history or streaming.

This program reads a question from the command-line arguments and an API key from the `CHAT_API_KEY` environment variable, sends the question as a single user message to a chat-completions endpoint at a placeholder URL (api.example.com) with a placeholder model name, and prints the text of the first answer returned. It needs console, environment, and HTTP access, and it fails with a clear error if the key is missing, the response has no choices, or the network or JSON handling goes wrong. Before relying on it, note that the endpoint and model are hardcoded placeholders you would have to change, and that it is a one-shot tool with no conversation history, retries, or streaming.

This program reads a question from the command-line arguments and an API key from the `CHAT_API_KEY` environment variable, posts the question as a single user message to a fixed chat-completions endpoint (with a placeholder model name), and prints the text of the first answer. It needs console, environment, and HTTP access, and it fails with a clear error if the key is missing, the response has no answer choices, or the network or JSON handling goes wrong. Before relying on it, note that the endpoint URL and model name are hard-coded examples you would have to change, and the code has a few spots that may not compile as written, such as `main` using `fail with` inside a `match` expression branch and the program declaring a top-level `let` constant.
